description: The main window. Least privilege (AGENTS.md): the app's own commands and nothing else. The job commands (D0), the browsing commands (D1), the staging commands (D2), the extract plan command (D3), the foreign-archive commands (D8: open, close, list, plan an extract; a password is sent once in the open call and kept only in Rust), the test, health, export, and repair setup commands (D4; the test and repair jobs themselves run through start_job), and the launch listener (D6: the shell's open, extract, and add verbs are handled in Rust; the webview only hears that an archive was opened or why a launch failed). The native dialogs (open, choose sources, save, choose an extract folder, choose an archive to test or repair, a copy, the new archive, a report file) are shown from Rust and dropped paths are received by Rust, so the webview never names a path: no fs, shell, http, or dialog permission is granted, and core:default is not granted. Also the passphrase and key-envelope commands (D5: unlock_archive and unlock_check_subject take a passphrase once into a zeroizing key session in Rust, cancel_unlock, list_envelopes; the create, rekey, and search jobs run through start_job). Also the update commands (T13, in-app updates: get_update_settings and set_update_settings read and change one opt-in switch, the check at start-up, which is off by default; check_for_update asks the fixed GitHub Releases endpoint, from Rust, whether a newer version exists and returns its version and release notes as text; the download and install run as the start_job kind install_update, only for the version check_for_update offered and only after the user confirms it, and the package signature is verified in Rust against the public key in tauri.conf.json before anything is installed. The webview is NOT granted any updater:* permission, makes no network request, and supplies no URL, so the CSP is unchanged.) Also open_user_guide (audit F8, Help, User guide): it takes no argument; Rust resolves the guide the installer bundles as a resource and hands it to the operating system's handler for .html, so the webview names no path and gets no fs, shell, or opener permission. The guide is static and offline. Also the simplified start screen (D10): recent_archives, open_recent, forget_recent_archives (the last archives opened; the webview sees file and folder names and opens an entry by its position, never a path), open_dropped_archive (a single .mochi file dropped on the window is held by Rust and opened on request), plan_extract_default and discard_extract_folder (extract into a new folder next to the archive, made and tidied up by Rust), and show_in_folder (Rust asks the operating system to show a folder it resolved itself). None takes or returns a path, and no fs, shell, or opener permission is granted. Also foreign_search (D8: the search box over an open ZIP, 7z, RAR, tar, tar.gz or tar.zst archive; it takes a handle, the text to look for and a case flag, matches entry names already held in Rust, never file contents, and returns rows, escaped paths and folder keys, so no path crosses and it is not a new permission class). Also stage_dropped_archive (a single archive file dropped on the window is held by Rust; this takes no argument and stages that held file as an ordinary source to add, exactly as a dropped file is staged, so no path crosses either way), and open_archive, open_recent and open_dropped_archive now open a foreign archive as well as a MOCHI one, deciding by the file in Rust, with a foreign archive that needs a password answered through open_foreign_archive. Also drag_out and drag_out_foreign (dragging selected entries out of an open archive into the file manager): the webview names only the archive handle, the snapshot, and the entry keys; Rust extracts them through the same restore engine as Extract into its own freshly made, randomly named, owner-only temporary folder under the app's cache directory (refused above 8 GiB declared, deleted when the drag is cancelled, and swept when more than an hour old), and starts the operating system's drag itself, so the webview never sees a path and no fs, shell, dialog, or drag plugin permission is granted.
